intro: Engineers build complex problem solving, systems analysis and sound judgment, and science, construction and management roles all need them. Of the 25 careers below, Materials Scientists match mechanical, civil and electrical engineers most closely at 80%, with a BLS May 2025 median of $117,790.
why_it_works: Engineering work means modeling how things behave, testing designs against limits and choosing the safest workable option. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 3.84 out of 5 across mechanical, civil and electrical engineers, so research, earth science and construction roles rank high. Construction managers apply the same planning to crews, schedules and budgets. Data and computing roles reuse your math and systems thinking. The gaps are mostly people skills, such as coordination and negotiation.
tips: Decide between going deeper or going broader: science roles reward technical depth, while management roles reward leading people and budgets.
Take on a project lead role at work to build the coordination and negotiation skills the top matches ask for.
Check whether a target role needs a graduate degree; 3 of the 25 matches usually do, including architecture.

faq.q: What jobs can engineers do besides engineering?
faq.a: The closest matches are Materials Scientists (80%), Architects, Except Landscape and Naval (79%) and Water Resource Specialists (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Construction Managers (78%) and Geoscientists, Except Hydrologists and Geographers (74%) are also close and use your design and analysis skills.

faq.q: Which careers pay more than engineering?
faq.a: 8 of the 25 matches pay more than the $106,520 median for the engineers on this page. Architectural and Engineering Managers earn $171,270 (+61%), Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470 (+38%) and Computer and Information Research Scientists earn $140,300 (+32%), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do engineers need another degree to change careers?
faq.a: Usually not. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than an engineering degree, based on O*NET Job Zones. 3 of them usually need a graduate degree, including Architects, Except Landscape and Naval, which also need a state license to practice.

faq.q: What engineering jobs are close to mechanical, civil or electrical work?
faq.a: If you want to stay in engineering but change focus, the nearest roles are Water/Wastewater Engineers (94% match), Industrial Engineers (92%), Transportation Engineers (92%) and Solar Energy Systems Engineers (90%). These keep your core training while moving into a different industry.
